meta.title: V2 - Move Material To The Red

modules.intro: V2 has to pass the same inspection V1 did. Check before you hand in.
modules.title: Still Legal
modules.aiNote: Unrestricted for driving SolidWorks. Measure in the model, do not eyeball it.

items: Saved as a new file. V1 still exists untouched
Anchor hole still 1.000 in, throat still 1.000 in clear to the edge
Center to center still between 2.000 and 2.500 in

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: V1 preserved, V2 saved separately, and all four dimensional checks hold.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: V2 exists but one dimensional rule is broken, or V1 was overwritten.

rubric.criterion: V2 is a separate file that still passes every dimensional rule

modules.intro: Yesterday's red spot is the whole brief. Two sentences per answer is plenty.
modules.title: What Changed, And Why
modules.aiNote: Ask it how to build a shape. Do not ask it what shape to build. The last question is about the assistant itself, so answer that one yourself.

blocks.content:
Upload one screenshot of V2. Mark the place you changed.

**Windows + Shift + S** to grab it, then **Ctrl + V** in any answer box below.

Every hook has a mass limit, so material you add somewhere is usually material you took from somewhere else. The last question is about that trade, and "I did not have to" is a real answer if you can say why.

blocks.prompt: What did you change, and where? Name the place on the part, and say whether it is the spot your simulation went red.
Why there? What do you expect it to do to the stress?
What did it cost you? Mass, material removed elsewhere, or nothing. Say why if it was nothing.
Did your SolidWorks assistant get anything wrong today? Paste any [MISS] lines it printed. If it never got anything wrong, just say so.

blocks.content:
### Sources

- Hook Design and Manufacturing Guide, Dimensions, Design and CAD, and Simulation tabs.
- Your V1 simulation study, run in the Simulation Lab.
- Shigley's Mechanical Engineering Design, 10th edition, Budynas and Nisbett, McGraw-Hill, 2015. Stress concentration and the effect of a fillet.
- IDEA AI Use Policy.

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Screenshot is of V2 and the changed area is marked.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Screenshot uploaded but nothing is marked, or it is a picture of V1.

rubric.criterion: Screenshot of V2 with the changed area marked

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Names where on the hook the change is and says whether it is where the study went red.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Says what changed but does not connect it to the simulation result.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Says something changed without saying where.

rubric.criterion: The change is located on the part and tied to the simulation result

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Explains why that location and what it should do to the stress there.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Gives a reason but no expected effect, or an effect with no reason.

levels.label: Absent
levels.descriptor: Nothing written, or a reason that is not about stress or strength.

rubric.criterion: Gives a reason for the change and a predicted effect on stress

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Names what the change cost, or argues convincingly that it cost nothing.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.descriptor: Says a cost or says none, without a reason.

rubric.criterion: Accounts for the trade the change required

levels.label: Complete
levels.descriptor: Pastes the [MISS] lines the assistant printed, or states plainly that it got nothing wrong. Both are full marks.

levels.label: Developing
levels.descriptor: Something is written but it does not say whether the assistant was wrong, or is too vague to act on.

rubric.criterion: Reports whether the assistant was wrong, either way
